The Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia, is a multi-purpose retractable roof stadium that serves as the home of the Atlanta Falcons of the National Football League (NFL) and Atlanta United FC of Major League Soccer (MLS). It has the world's largest halo board and is one of five NFL stadiums with a retractable roof. The stadium was opened in August 2017, but the retractable roof system was not completed until July 2018. The original design featured an eight-panel retractable roof that resembles a pinwheel and a glass wall that opens with the roof to allow in fresh air. The stadium is owned by the state of Georgia through the Georgia World Congress Center Authority and operated by AMB Group, the parent organization of the Falcons and Atlanta United. The total cost of the stadium was estimated at $1.6 billion. The stadium also includes a 100-yard bar, a fantasy football lounge, and premium club seating at field level.
